title: Timothy Joins Paul, Lydia's Conversion, Paul and Silas in Prison

questions.question: Timothy's mother was a Jewish believer, but his father was a Greek. Why did Paul circumcise him?
options: Because of the Jews in those places, who knew that his father was Greek
Because Timothy had not yet been circumcised as an infant
Because the Jerusalem council now required it for all converts
Because it was a condition set by the Lystra church elders
questions.correctAnswer: Because of the Jews in those places, who knew that his father was Greek
questions.explanation: Acts 16:3 (ESV): "Paul wanted Timothy to accompany him, and he took him and circumcised him because of the Jews who were in those places, for they all knew that his father was a Greek."

questions.question: Paul and his companions were forbidden by the Holy Spirit to speak the word in Asia and were not allowed to go into Bithynia. Where did they go instead?
options: Down to Troas
Back to Antioch
Into Galatia again
Toward Macedonia directly
questions.explanation: Acts 16:8 (ESV): "So, passing by Mysia, they went down to Troas."

questions.question: At Troas, Paul had a vision of a man of Macedonia urging him to come over and help them. What did the team conclude this meant?
options: God had called them to preach the gospel to Macedonia
The Holy Spirit was leading them to a new territory
There was a great need for teachers in that region
A new door of ministry was opening in Europe
questions.correctAnswer: God had called them to preach the gospel to Macedonia
questions.explanation: Acts 16:10 (ESV): "And when Paul had seen the vision, immediately we sought to go on into Macedonia, concluding that God had called us to preach the gospel to them."

questions.question: In Philippi, on the Sabbath, they went outside the city gate to a riverside where they expected to find a place of prayer. Who was among those gathered there?
options: Lydia, a seller of purple goods from the city of Thyatira, who was a worshipper of God
Priscilla and Aquila, recently arrived from Rome
A Roman centurion named Cornelius who worshipped God
The jailer's wife, who had heard of Jesus of Nazareth
questions.correctAnswer: Lydia, a seller of purple goods from the city of Thyatira, who was a worshipper of God
questions.explanation: Acts 16:14 (ESV): "One who heard us was a woman named Lydia, from the city of Thyatira, a seller of purple goods, who was a worshiper of God."

questions.question: What opened Lydia's heart to pay attention to what Paul said?
options: The Lord opened her heart
The signs Paul performed convinced her
The Scriptures she had studied persuaded her
The testimony of the other women at the riverside
questions.explanation: Acts 16:14 (ESV): "The Lord opened her heart to pay attention to what was said by Paul."

questions.question: A slave girl with a spirit of divination kept following Paul, crying out: "These men are servants of the Most High God, who proclaim to you the way of salvation." How many days did this continue?
options: Many days
Seven days
Three days
Forty days
questions.explanation: Acts 16:18 (ESV): "And this she kept doing for many days."

questions.question: After Paul cast the spirit out of the slave girl, why were her owners furious?
options: Their hope of gain from her fortune-telling was gone
They feared the Roman authorities would blame them
They had not given permission for Paul to heal her
They did not want her to join the new Christian sect
questions.correctAnswer: Their hope of gain from her fortune-telling was gone
questions.explanation: Acts 16:19 (ESV): "But when her owners saw that their hope of gain was gone, they seized Paul and Silas and dragged them into the marketplace before the rulers."

questions.question: Paul and Silas were beaten with rods and thrown into the inner prison, their feet fastened in the stocks. What were they doing at midnight?
options: Praying and singing hymns to God, while the other prisoners were listening
Calling out to God to deliver them from their chains
Weeping and asking God why they were allowed to suffer
Preaching to the other prisoners about the resurrection
questions.correctAnswer: Praying and singing hymns to God, while the other prisoners were listening
questions.explanation: Acts 16:25 (ESV): "About midnight Paul and Silas were praying and singing hymns to God, and the prisoners were listening to them."

questions.question: A great earthquake shook the foundations of the prison. All the doors opened and everyone's bonds were unfastened. The jailer, thinking the prisoners had escaped, was about to kill himself when Paul cried out what?
options: "Do not harm yourself, for we are all here."
"We have not fled; God kept us here for you."
"Stop! The Lord has a message for you tonight."
"Your life is worth more than your post, friend."
questions.correctAnswer: "Do not harm yourself, for we are all here."
questions.explanation: Acts 16:28 (ESV): "But Paul cried with a loud voice, 'Do not harm yourself, for we are all here.'"

questions.question: The jailer fell trembling before Paul and Silas and asked: "Sirs, what must I do to be saved?" What was their answer?
options: "Believe in the Lord Jesus, and you will be saved, you and your household."
"Repent and be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ."
"Confess your sins and turn from your wicked ways."
"Accept Jesus as Lord and submit to baptism this night."
questions.correctAnswer: "Believe in the Lord Jesus, and you will be saved, you and your household."
questions.explanation: Acts 16:31 (ESV): "And they said, 'Believe in the Lord Jesus, and you will be saved, you and your household.'"

questions.question: After the jailer and his household were baptized, what did he do for Paul and Silas?
options: He took them and washed their wounds and set food before them, and rejoiced with his household
He released them immediately and accompanied them to Lydia's house
He reported to his superiors that the prisoners were still in custody
He brought them new clothing and a generous gift of money
questions.correctAnswer: He took them and washed their wounds and set food before them, and rejoiced with his household
questions.explanation: Acts 16:33-34 (ESV): "And he took them the same hour of the night and washed their wounds; and he was baptized at once, he and all his family. Then he brought them up into his house and set food before them. And he rejoiced along with his entire household that he had believed in God."

questions.question: Why did Paul refuse to simply leave when the magistrates sent officers to release him?
options: He declared they were Roman citizens who had been beaten publicly without a trial and demanded the magistrates come themselves to release them
He insisted they had the right to an official apology before leaving
He was waiting for the full church to gather and witness their release
He demanded written assurance that the Philippian church would not be harassed
questions.correctAnswer: He declared they were Roman citizens who had been beaten publicly without a trial and demanded the magistrates come themselves to release them
questions.explanation: Acts 16:37 (ESV): "But Paul said to them, 'They have beaten us publicly, uncondemned, men who are Roman citizens, and have thrown us into prison; and do they now throw us out secretly?...'..."

questions.question: Lydia urged Paul and his team after her baptism. What did she say?
options: "If you have judged me to be faithful to the Lord, come to my house and stay." And she prevailed upon them.
"Let my home be your home for as long as you remain in Macedonia."
"Please accept this gift for your work and stay as long as needed."
"I will provide everything needed for your ministry here in Philippi."
questions.correctAnswer: "If you have judged me to be faithful to the Lord, come to my house and stay." And she prevailed upon them.
questions.explanation: Acts 16:15 (ESV): "...she urged us, saying, 'If you have judged me to be faithful to the Lord, come to my house and stay.' And she prevailed upon us."

questions.question: Paul and Silas visited Lydia and the brothers before departing Philippi. What did they do there?
options: They encouraged them and departed
They prayed and shared the Lord's Supper
They commissioned new elders for the church
They wrote a letter to be sent to Antioch
questions.explanation: Acts 16:40 (ESV): "So they went out of the prison and visited Lydia. And when they had seen the brothers, they encouraged them and departed."

questions.question: The charges brought against Paul and Silas in Philippi were that they were "Jews who are disturbing our city. They advocate customs that are not lawful for us as Romans to accept or practice." Which of these facts is noteworthy?
options: Philippi was a Roman colony with proud Roman citizenship rights, making this an especially serious charge
The charges were brought in the Latin language rather than Greek
The accusation fulfilled a prophecy Paul had received at Troas
The beating was carried out by the Jewish community, not the Romans
questions.correctAnswer: Philippi was a Roman colony with proud Roman citizenship rights, making this an especially serious charge
questions.explanation: Acts 16:12,20-21 (ESV): "...Philippi, which is a leading city of the district of Macedonia and a Roman colony..." The Roman colony status made Paul's claim of Roman citizenship particularly powerful.

key_verse_text: "Believe in the Lord Jesus, and you will be saved, you and your household."
